correctness.rationale: All n>=3 and tau>0: real Fourier basis and rectangular Gram identity give the determinant exactly. Sine product and gcd characterize rank. Nonzero h_0m follows coefficientwise from Lagrange polynomials at strictly positive, ordered nodes; SPD inverse temporal Gram ensures strict gap. Independent exact integer Bareiss checker verifies 96 cases, genuine exponential heat kernel checker 35 cases. These are proof stress tests, not a finite substitute for the universal argument.

originality.rationale: The primary 2011 cycle observability paper and full-text 2014/2016 log-determinant sensor-placement literature do not establish the explicit finite-time two-sensor determinant or its odd/even D-optimality classification. The closest published cycle result optimizes a spectrally demixed frame norm, not the untreated observation Gramian; the cross-frequency temporal inverse-Gram interaction is a substantive missing step. General Fourier and Vandermonde tools are known and not claimed as new. Residual risk is a specialized prior exact formula elsewhere.
residual_risks: Historical specialized exact cyclic D-optimality formula outside inspected works could overlap; searches cannot establish uniqueness.
The original 2011 paper has parity-specific observability criteria; the present proof derives its rank criterion independently and does not assert correction of that source.
Observation normalization, positive distinct heat eigenvalues, and fixed r+1 observation count are essential; no extension to noise-colored or arbitrary weighted graphs.

value.rationale: Finite-horizon D-optimal state observability is naturally about determinant, unlike qualitative rank or demixed spectral frame conditioning. A complete closed-form family for all cycle orders and heat times is an operational sensor-placement classification; odd-cycle coprime ties and the strict observable-but-suboptimal even-order alternative expose a nontrivial time-frequency interaction. The n=6,d=2 witness shows the distinction concretely and motivates use of the exact objective.
